body: Since this comes up every round, I ran the five that get recommended here on the same rig so the numbers are at least comparable. Coupler is a 5128-779, same pad seating each time, 30 minutes settling.\n\nThe short version: the two everybody argues about are 62 ohms and 98.6 dB/mW, which is why one of them goes loud enough off a phone and the other does not, and it is nothing to do with the driver being 'harder to drive'. The rest of the spread is smaller than the pad variation, which is the actual point of the post: if you have not matched pads you have not compared anything.

Pad swap list, because three people have asked this round.\n\nThe pads that fit are XP934-NS for the older cups and PD122-UH for the ones with the moulded lip -- they look identical in photographs and they are not, the lip one is 2mm deeper at the rear and will sit crooked on the older cup. Neither is listed on the maker's own site any more; the distributor still stocks both under those numbers if you email rather than use the web form. Do not buy the generic ones, the mounting ring is a different diameter and it tears.

For anyone whose driver has gone rattly out of warranty: it is worth one email before you write them off.\n\nDo not go through the shop. The distributor handles service directly and their service address takes an RMA request without a dealer reference if you quote the distributor code EU/888946 and ask for a goodwill assessment. Mine was four years old and out of warranty and they replaced the driver for the cost of the postage. RMA came back as X4385228 -- quoting a previous one seems to help, so use it.
